title: Labels and the table
subtitle: Reading Rioja and eating with it

steps.title: Reading the label
steps.body: Rioja labels show the producer, the vintage, the category, Crianza, Reserva or Gran Reserva, and sometimes the zone, village or Viñedo Singular. The back label carries the Consejo Regulador seal. Cosecha or Genérico wines don't follow the ageing ladder and may be young or modern.

steps.title: At the table
steps.body: Rioja suits lamb, especially chuletillas, small lamb chops grilled over vine cuttings; roast suckling pig; chorizo; jamón ibérico; and Manchego. Gran Reserva suits mushrooms, game and stews. Crianza suits tapas. White Rioja suits fish and oxidative styles suit aged cheese.

steps.prompt: Which dish is a Rioja classic?
options: Lamb chops grilled over vine cuttings

steps.body: An old Gran Reserva may throw sediment. Stand it up for a day and decant gently; its pale colour is normal.

steps.prompt: A pale, garnet colour in old Gran Reserva is a fault.
steps.explanation: Not true. Long oak and bottle ageing naturally lighten the colour.

steps.title: What you learned
points: Labels show category, seal and sometimes place
Rioja suits lamb, jamón and Manchego
Old Gran Reservas are pale, mellow and best decanted gently
